Constant connectivity can weaken attention and reduce face to face interaction. Social media may spread misinformation quickly and encourage harmful comparison. Automation can replace some jobs, requiring workers to develop new skills. Privacy is another concern, since companies and institutions collect vast amounts of personal information. Technology itself is neither wholly beneficial nor harmful. Its impact depends on how people design, regulate, and use it. Schools can teach digital literacy, governments can protect data, and businesses can prioritize human wellbeing. Individuals can set healthy boundaries and question what they encounter online. When innovation is guided by responsibility and inclusion, technology can expand opportunity and improve quality of life. Society should welcome advances while staying alert to their costs and consequences.
